after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis and its velocity at time $t>0$ is given by $v(t)=3{t}^{2}-6t.$ 
At time $t=2,$ the particle is located at the position $x=6.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=5?$
after.worked_solution:
The position of the particle at $t=5$ is equal to its position at $t=2$ plus the total displacement over $t\in [2,5].$ Therefore, we can calculate it as follows:

$$
x(5)=x(2)+{\int }_{2}^{5}v(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

Carrying out the computations, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(5) & =6+{\int }_{2}^{5}(3{t}^{2}-6t)\,\text{dt} \\  & =6+{[{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}]}_{2}^{5} \\  & =6+([(5)^{3}-3(5)^{2}]-[(2)^{3}-3(2)^{2}]) \\  & =6+([125-75]-[8-12]) \\  & =6+(50-(-4)) \\  & =6+54 \\  & =60.\end{aligned}
$$

So the position of the particle at $t=5$ is $x=60.$

after.problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis and its velocity at time $t>0$ is given by $v(t)=4t+3{t}^{2}.$ At time $t=1$ the particle is located at the position $x=12.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=4?$

$$
x(4)=x(1)+{\int }_{1}^{4}v(t)\,\text{d}t

$$
\begin{aligned}x(4) & =12+{\int }_{1}^{4}(4t+3{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & =12+[2{t}^{2}+{t}^{3}]_{1}^{4} \\  & =12+([2(4)^{2}+{4}^{3}]-[2(1)^{2}+{1}^{3}]) \\  & =12+([32+64]-[2+1]) \\  & =12+(96-3) \\  & =12+93 \\  & =105\end{aligned}

decision.explanation: From t=2 to t=4, displacement is the rectangle area 2·4=8. From t=4 to t=7, it is the triangle area (1/2)·3·4=6. Velocity is zero from t=7 to t=8. Therefore x(8)=1+8+6=15.

The graph above shows the velocity of an object moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis. At time $t=2$ the particle is located at the position $x=1.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=8?$
after.worked_solution:
The position of the particle at $t=8$ is equal to its position at $t=2$ plus the total displacement over $t\in [2,8].$ Therefore, we can calculate it as follows:

$$
x(8)=x(2)+{\int }_{2}^{8}v(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

We are told that $x(2)=1$, and we can compute the integral ${\int }_{2}^{8}v(t)\,\text{d}t$ by finding the signed area under the graph from $t=2$ to $t=8.$ Computing the signed area, we get

$$
{\int }_{2}^{8}v(t)\,\text{d}t=14.
$$

Therefore,

$$
x(8)=1+14=15
$$

So the position of the particle at $t=8$ is $x=15.$

after.worked_solution:
The position of the particle at $t=6$ is equal to its position at $t=3$ plus the total displacement over $t\in [3,6].$ Therefore, we can calculate it as follows:

$$
x(6)=x(3)+{\int }_{3}^{6}v(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

Carrying out the computations, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(6) & =2+{\int }_{3}^{6}(6t-{t}^{2})\,\text{d}t \\  & =2+{[3{t}^{2}-\frac{1}{3}{t}^{3}]}_{3}^{6} \\  & =2+[3(6)^{2}-\frac{1}{3}(6)^{3}]-[3(3)^{2}-\frac{1}{3}(3)^{3}] \\  & =2+36-18 \\  & =2+18 \\  & =20.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the position of the particle at $t=6$ is $x=20.$
